answer: Identity is split across two 11.6 POA bonds planted 400 meters apart: one on a surveyed lagoon berm, one in a numbered meadow strip. For 18 days the pair jointly signs a 5-byte sighting only in the 90-second window when a public beacon hits solar zenith. Auditors recompute both site IDs from the epoch seed; a second bond on the same berm or strip, a missed zenith window, or a one-site signature burns the bonds and locks those keys for 12 epochs. Spinning up 2,000 aliases would need 4,000 unshared sites and 36,000 on-time co-signatures. A reused sighting chain voids both identities at once.
